instruction.text: Find the white, fluffy parts of the cotton plant to learn a fun fact.

feedback.end: This is a cotton plant. The white, fluffy fibres are woven into yarn that we use to make clothing.

instruction.text: Find the sheep’s fleece to learn a fun fact.

hint.text: Fleece is the word for sheep’s hair.

feedback.end: Every year, farmers cut the fleece of sheep and turn it into wool, which can be used to produce things like clothing and blankets.

instruction.text: Find the tree trunk to learn a fun fact.

feedback.end: Trees are cut down and their wood is used to make things like furniture, toys and even pencils. Can you see anything made of wood around you?

instruction.text: Find the rock to learn a fun fact.

feedback.end: In many rocks, there are metals like iron, gold or aluminium. With a lot of work, we can pull these metals from the rock and turn them into something else, for example cans or cars.
